## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mittākāḷītherīgāthā* (Thig 5.6) is a poetic discourse preserved in the *Therīgāthā* section of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. Attributed to the bhikkhunī Mittākāḷī, the verses recount her spiritual journey: having gone forth into homelessness inspired by faith, she subsequently experienced a period of spiritual lapse or dryness, being lured by gifts and worldly honours and neglecting the path of insight [Horner 1930]. Urged by the realization that life is short and subject to decay from sickness and aging, she renounced indolence and vigorously contemplated the arising and passing away of the aggregates [Blackstone 2000; Evans-Wentz et al. 2000]. Through this direct contemplation, she won liberation and arahantship, declaring that the Buddha's teaching had been accomplished [Horner 1930; Blackstone 2000; Evans-Wentz et al. 2000].

Text-reuse data from DharmaNexus shows that the poem shares six matching textual segments (§0.3–6.1) with its traditional commentary, the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus identifies low-scoring matches with the Tibetan *Jātakanidāna* (D0032), though no established parallels are listed in canonical records [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The text is preserved across numerous modern renderings, including English translations by C.A.F. Rhys Davids, Bhikkhu Sujato, and Ayya Soma [SuttaCentral; Evans-Wentz et al. 2000].
